sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Light Value-Added Postponement Packaging and Custom Kitting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (cross-strait investor origin for a mainland China WFOE; the corporate seat and operational jurisdiction are in mainland China)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (civil-law jurisdictions; mainland China governs WFOE formation and Taiwan governs the investing entity; cross-strait investment overlay applies)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion
Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Enhancement of Tax Cooperation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation, Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Business Registration Department
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public -> Taiwan District Court notarization -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) notarization -> Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification -> PRC notary/SAMR acceptance. This is the exclusive consular-legalization-equivalent cross-strait path; no Hague Apostille may be added. If an investor document originates from an Apostille Convention state, the parallel exclusive path is notarization plus Apostille directly, never combined with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan MOEA (Commerce/Corporate Affairs Office) or local business registration authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same Taiwan SEF/ARATS verification chain as above; a Hague Apostille is not available for Taiwan documents and must not be chained. For Apostille Convention states, obtain a fresh Apostille from the competent authority in place of any consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing WFOE incorporation and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan investing company (notarized by Taiwan notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary -> District Court -> SEF -> ARATS -> onward delivery to PRC notary/SAMR and banks. In parallel for non-Taiwan parties: notarize and apostille; do not send the same instrument through both SEF/ARATS and apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles) of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investing company as registered/amended with the Taiwan MOEA or provincial-level corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy from Taiwan MOEA, notarized and passed through SEF/ARATS verification for PRC use. For an Apostille Convention-state parent, certify and apostille the issued copy; apostille and consular legalization are alternate, mutually exclusive routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank maintaining the investor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank official signature plus Taiwan notary and SEF/ARATS verification for PRC acceptance. Apostille route applies to bank letters from Apostille Convention states; never use consular legalization in addition to an apostille for the same letter.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All direct owners, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened against the PBOC terrorist and designated-person lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK sanctions, and China's judicial/administrative enforcement databases. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including Taiwanese ministers, legislators, state-owned enterprise executives, military commanders, and senior judicial officials, require enhanced due diligence covering source of wealth, source of funds, and public-office history for at least 12 months after leaving office. Any positive hit must be escalated to the AML compliance officer, documented in the UBO register, and resolved by freezing the relevant transaction and suspending incorporation until clearance from competent authorities. Screening is refreshed within 24 hours of any sanctions-list update.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (www.gsxt.gov.cn) and the SAMR Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration Platform (administered locally by the provincial/municipal Market Regulation Administration)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must use simplified Chinese characters; pinyin or romanized letter names are not registered legal names. The four-tier naming structure is mandatory: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business description (for example, fulfillment packaging, supply-chain management) + organizational form (limited company). The administrative-division tier may be omitted only if central approval is obtained. A Chinese name may include an English sanctioned counterpart only for banking/customs convenience, but it does not replace the statutory Chinese name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant should first analyze the rejection reasons in the SAMR portal, modify the distinctive token or industry phrase, and re-declare. If the rejection is believed erroneous, the applicant or its counsel may submit an administrative reconsideration application to the decision-making Market Regulation Administration's immediate superior within 60 days of the rejection notice. The application must attach the original rejection notice, the name-declaration screenshot, the proposed English translation, and a legal memorandum. If the applicant remains aggrieved after reconsideration, it may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within 6 months. A one-time 30-day extension of a valid name reservation may be requested before expiry where the local SAMR module permits; otherwise the name must be reserved afresh.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox arrangements are not permissible for this WFOE because the fulfillment kitting and 3PL assembly scope requires an operating warehouse and actual business premises. The PRC tax authorities and bank account-opening officers require a physical registered address where the lease, property ownership certificate, utility bills, payroll, inventory, and board documents can be inspected. A mail-only address will trigger SAMR 'abnormal operation' listing, tax address rejection, and bank refusal to open the corporate account. The applicant may use an office/warehouse lease with an attached front office as the registered address; a pure virtual mailbox cannot satisfy commercial substance for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 70% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months after incorporation. Checklist for on-site readiness: (i) original lease deed and property ownership certificate; (ii) a visible company name plate and chop book; (iii) employees physically present during business hours; (iv) warehouse racking, packing tables, scales, kitting supplies, and inventory records; (v) board resolution approving the lease and business scope; (vi) tax registration and able-to-issue electronic invoice system installed at the address; (vii) payroll, social insurance, and attendance records; (viii) AML/CFT internal control manual and UBO filing receipt; (ix) fire safety inspection certificate for the warehouse; (x) third-party logistics contracts or customer fulfillment orders.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government name clearance and business license registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SAMR and local Market Regulation Administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Legislated zero-official-fee policy; no statutory tariff for name declaration or company registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal set (company chop, financial chop, invoice chop, legal representative chop) and engraving
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed seal engraving vendor registered with the Ministry of Public Security
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Shenzhen/Shanghai market benchmark of USD 60-180 for a four-chop set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taiwan notarization of investor corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan notary public and Taiwan District Court notarization office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Taiwan notarial fee schedule; USD 200-400 for the corporate document package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SEF and ARATS cross-strait document verification fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cross-strait administrative fee schedule; estimated USD 120-250 per bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille fees for any investor documents issued in an Apostille Convention state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin (e.g., U.S. state Secretary of State, UK FCDO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention fee schedule; USD 50-250 per instrument depending on jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered physical office and warehouse arrangement (first month occupancy cost allocated to pre-incorporation registered address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a small 3PL front office and warehouse in Shenzhen/Shanghai outer districts; USD 400-1,200 per month

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC legal counsel for drafting Articles, Board Resolutions, Power of Attorney, UBO filing and AML/CFT internal controls
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC law firm with foreign-related and cross-strait practice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for WFOE incorporation plus UBO and AML compliance; USD 1,800-4,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Independent AML/KYC PEP and sanctions screening databases and UBO risk-scoring service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for entity onboarding screening; USD 250-500 for subscription and automated checks

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, including Articles 17-18, 128-156, 156-169, 170-177, and 387; Foreign Investment Act, including Articles 4, 7, 8, 10, and 12; Business Registration Act, including Articles 3, 17, and 18.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent municipal/county government company-registration authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (公司登記申請書), accompanied, where applicable, by the Foreign Investment Approval Application and foreign-invested capital verification documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan has no general statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited company. The subscribed capital must be sufficient for the proposed business and establishment costs. Foreign investment capital must be remitted through an authorized Taiwanese bank into the approved investment structure and verified by a Taiwan-certified public accountant. A statutory escrow account is not generally required, although the bank may require a temporary capital account before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the Company accept the subscription by its foreign shareholder for all issued capital specified in the approved investment application, subject to lawful remittance and certified capital verification. Resolved that the registered office at the address approved by the competent authority is adopted as the Company’s principal office. Resolved that [Name] is appointed Director and authorized representative, [Name] is appointed Manager, and [Name] is appointed responsible officer for tax, banking, labor, and regulatory filings. The authorized representative may execute all incorporation, banking, investment, lease, and licensing documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Business Scope, Premises, and Foreign Investment Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce; Investment Review Administration; and the relevant local government business-registration counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that fulfillment, storage, packing, labeling, and light kitting activities are accurately classified in the proposed business scope. Verify land-use, building-use, warehouse, traffic, fire, and environmental compatibility before signing a long-term lease. Confirm that the proposed foreign shareholder and beneficial owners are not subject to investment restrictions or sanctions.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese company name and business scope
Passport or corporate-registration documents of foreign directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace restricted business codes, correct the proposed company name or premises classification, and resubmit the preliminary review with a written response to each authority query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company and Business One-Stop Service portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online name and business-scope precheck using the intended limited-company form. Use Taiwan business classification codes corresponding to logistics support, warehousing, packing, labeling, or other permitted activities. Do not describe regulated manufacturing, customs brokerage, food handling, pharmaceuticals, or hazardous-material operations unless separately approved.
required_dossiers: Chinese translations of foreign corporate documents, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit alternative Chinese names, remove ambiguous or restricted business items, and file a corrected precheck application within the validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Review Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign investment application before capital remittance. Provide the investment plan, ownership chain, source-of-funds explanation, proposed capital, business scope, directors, beneficial-owner information, and premises evidence. Foreign documents must be notarized or certified in their place of issuance, authenticated or legalized as required, translated into Chinese, and submitted in the prescribed form.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation or equivalent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the review memorandum, provide missing ownership or source-of-funds evidence, amend the investment plan, or withdraw and refile if the proposed activity is restricted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles and Establish the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company registration window of the competent local government or Ministry of Economic Affairs online company-registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the Articles of Incorporation, appoint directors and the responsible person, obtain the registered-office consent, and complete any required founder signatures. Foreign execution documents must be notarized, authenticated or legalized, and translated. Open the temporary capital account where required by the bank, remit the approved capital, and obtain a Taiwan-certified public accountant capital-verification report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure formal deficiencies, replace non-compliant documents, correct capital or address information, and resubmit before the application is finally rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Bank, Labor, and Beneficial-Owner Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, local tax office, authorized bank, Ministry of Labor systems, and the competent company-registration authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the unified business number and complete tax registration. Convert the temporary capital account into the operating account, register the company seal and authorized signatory, and maintain accounting books in accordance with Taiwan law. Register labor insurance, employment insurance, and labor-pension obligations before hiring employees. Maintain required beneficial-owner and corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax, bank, or labor filings, provide enhanced due-diligence documents, and respond to any bank or authority compliance hold before commencing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Premises, Fire, Environmental, and Operational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant municipal or county Fire Department, Building Administration Office, Environmental Protection Bureau, Labor Inspection Office, and local industrial or commercial authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before occupying or operating the facility, confirm building-use legality, fire-protection equipment, evacuation routes, electrical loading, storage configuration, occupational safety, waste contracts, and any wastewater, air-emission, noise, or hazardous-material requirements. Obtain permits only where the facility or equipment triggers statutory thresholds.
required_dossiers: Building-use certificate and approved floor plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify physical deficiencies, commission a licensed professional inspection, revise the facility layout, obtain the required environmental or fire permit, and request reinspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, together with the relevant municipal or county government industrial and commercial authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Company Registration Certificate and Business Registration Certificate; no separate general manufacturing license is normally required for ordinary fulfillment, packing, labeling, and custom-kitting activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Ministry of Environment, Taiwan, and the relevant local Environmental Protection Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for ordinary leased warehousing and light kitting, subject to site location, development scale, land-use category, and equipment-specific screening under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with the Water Pollution Control Act and applicable discharge standards; air emissions and VOCs must comply with the Air Pollution Control Act and any applicable permit conditions; general and industrial waste must be segregated, stored, documented, and handled under the Waste Disposal Act by authorized contractors. Dust, noise, wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-material thresholds may trigger facility permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must satisfy local fire-safety inspection requirements, including alarms, extinguishers, emergency lighting, evacuation routes, and fire compartments. Building Administration authorities may require confirmation of lawful use, structural capacity, floor loading, racking, electrical systems, and alterations. The employer must implement occupational health and safety controls under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, conduct risk assessments, train workers, maintain safe material-handling procedures, and complete any required labor inspection or equipment certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA; 国家税务总局) — official portal www.chinatax.gov.cn; day-to-day registration, invoice and filing operations are executed through the province-level Electronic Tax Bureau (电子税务局) consolidated on the National Unified Electronic Tax Bureau platform (全国统一规范电子税务局); customs-export data matching and refund declaration run through China Electronic Port (中国电子口岸/出口退税申报系统).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CN WFOE obtains its Unified Social Credit Code (USCC, 统一社会信用代码) from the provincial Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) at incorporation. Within 30 calendar days after the business license is issued, the entity must complete initial tax registration confirmation (登记信息确认) via the Electronic Tax Bureau; the USCC automatically becomes the taxpayer identification number (TIN) used for Enterprise Income Tax (EIT), VAT, Individual Income Tax (IIT) payroll withholding, stamp duty and social insurance. A foreign investor that contracts directly in China without a business license must first obtain a temporary tax registration (临时税务登记) from the local STA office. The WFOE then files the VAT payer-status determination (general vs. small-scale), IIT withholding registration, payroll/social insurance linkage and electronic invoice quota calibration before issuing any invoice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The PRC WFOE is a resident enterprise (居民企业) under Article 2 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law (2007, as amended) and is taxed on worldwide income at the headline 25.0% CIT rate; territorial scope is global, with unilateral foreign tax credit relief (EIT Law Art. 23) available for Taiwan-source and other foreign taxes because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement (signed 25 Aug 2015) is not yet in force. The Taiwan investor is non-resident for PRC tax purposes; dividends and interest remitted from the WFOE are subject to 10.0% PRC withholding (reducible only if the cross-strait agreement is implemented or a local preferential policy applies; no treaty benefits are currently available). Tax-Exempt_Zone aspects: integrated bonded zones (综合保税区) treat goods entering the zone as exported (VAT exempt/zero-rated until the goods leave the zone into the PRC domestic market), and the Hainan Free Trade Port offers a 15% CIT rate for qualifying encouraged industries — relevant if the fulfillment/kitting operation is relocated into such zones.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: PRC law contains no check-the-box election: legal classification follows SAMR registration. The following statutory elections are relevant: (1) VAT payer-status election — an entity with annual taxable sales of RMB 5,000,000 or less may elect simplified small-scale registration (3% levy, temporarily reduced to 1% through 31 Dec 2027); above that threshold, general-taxpayer status is mandatory with full input-credit refunds; (2) deemed-resident election (actual management place test) may pull an offshore entity into PRC CIT; (3) small low-profit enterprise (小型微利企业) election lowers the effective CIT rate to 5% for annual taxable income up to RMB 3,000,000 subject to employee/asset caps; (4) high-and-new-technology enterprise certification (15% CIT) is available for qualifying technology-enabled fulfillment software; (5) no fiscal-unity/grouping election exists for CIT; (6) foreign tax credit may be elected on a per-country (direct and indirect) basis; (7) export-refund method is statutory, not elective: manufacturing-related exporters use the 免抵退税 method, trading exporters use the 免退税 method, and bonded-zone operators use the entry-into-zone deemed-export rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT; 增值税) administered by the STA, supplemented by urban maintenance and construction tax (7% of VAT paid in urban areas), education surcharges (3% + 2% local education surcharge) and stamp duty; the WFOE's sales of kitted goods, warehousing, packaging and fulfillment services are within VAT scope in the province where the fulfillment center is located.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory general-taxpayer registration applies once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 (net of VAT); taxpayers at or below this threshold may register as small-scale taxpayers (levy method: 3%, temporarily 1% until 31 Dec 2027); monthly sales of RMB 100,000 or less for small-scale taxpayers are VAT-exempt. Registration must be filed in the tax district of the operational warehouse/fulfillment address within 30 days of the trigger event; any VAT liability generates monthly/quarterly filing obligations via the Electronic Tax Bureau.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices (数电票) under the Golden Tax Phase IV system (金税四期). General taxpayers issue exclusively through the National Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform (电子发票服务平台): invoices are transmitted in real time to the STA, carry a unique 20-digit electronic invoice number, are cleared against the taxpayer's VAT ledger before offsets are computed, and are verified on the National VAT Invoice Verification Platform (全国增值税发票查验平台). There is no physical fiscal stamp, but the platform acts as a real-time clearance engine; API integration (电子税务局接口) is mandatory for high-volume issuers, and abnormal invoices (异常扣税凭证), red-letter reversal invoices (红字发票) and cross-zone issuance are flagged automatically for risk control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A general VAT taxpayer may apply the export zero rate (免征增值税并退还进项税额) where goods are physically exported through PRC customs under a lawful customs declaration, the WFOE holds title/control over the goods, the sale is made to an overseas buyer, and proceeds are collected in foreign currency or RMB from the buyer. For ISIC 5210 kitting/packaging: value-added processing incorporated into the exported goods price is refundable to the extent the final invoice classifies the supply as goods; standalone warehousing, handling and logistics services are domestic services at 6% VAT unless they qualify as zero-rated or VAT-exempt offshore/export services under the cross-border service rules (财税〔2016〕36号文 Annex IV, e.g., international freight forwarding, storage of goods located outside China, or services consumed entirely outside China). E-commerce export retail may use the exemption-without-refund regime for qualifying small parcels (cross-border e-commerce comprehensive pilot zones). Input VAT attributable to domestic services and overheads is apportioned and may be non-refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) reconciled through China Electronic Port (中国电子口岸) export data exchange
Export contract, commercial invoice and packing list (出口合同、商业发票、装箱单)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (海运提单或航空运单) evidencing physical exit of the goods
Bank inward remittance certificate / export FX collection record (银行收汇凭证或出口收汇监测系统记录; formerly 出口收汇核销单) showing receipt of the sales proceeds from the overseas buyer
Export invoice issued under the general taxpayer's invoice quota (出口发票) with prices aligned to the customs declaration value
3PL/fulfillment service agreement and kitting assembly records demonstrating that the value-added processing is embedded in the exported goods
Certificate of Origin or export-license waiver documents where goods are subject to export control or preferential origin claims
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export refund claims are risk-classified by the STA (Class I to IV); Class III and IV exporters are refunded only after manual verification. On fraud or error, the STA retroactively clawbacks the refunded VAT plus daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the refund date, and imposes an administrative penalty of 100%–500% of the defrauded amount under Article 66 of the Tax Collection Administration Law (2001, as amended). Criminal liability attaches under Article 204 of the Criminal Law (骗取出口退税罪) where the false refund exceeds RMB 50,000: up to 5 years imprisonment for substantial amounts, 5–10 years for large amounts (≥ RMB 500,000), and 10 years to life imprisonment with a fine of 1–5× the defrauded amount or confiscation of property for especially large amounts (≥ RMB 2.5 million). The Golden Tax IV abnormal-refund blocking mechanism triggers cross-agency review by STA, customs and SAFE whenever invoice, customs, FX settlement or logistics data do not fully reconcile; repeat offenders face suspension of export-refund eligibility for up to 3 years and placement on the serious-tax-violation public list with associated customs AEO sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) serving as the delegated authority for foreign-exchange supervision, approval, and registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is fully convertible under the current account for bona fide trade in goods and services, including cross-border payments arising from warehouse and fulfillment services. A Chinese WFOE can convert and remit trade-related receipts through designated banks upon submission of underlying contracts, invoices, tax evidence, and customs records. The capital account remains restricted: FDI capital injections, foreign debt, and external conversions require SAFE registration and the use of specially designated capital settlement accounts. Profit remittance is permitted only after annual audit, accrual of statutory reserves, and payment or withholding of income tax; banks must obtain evidence of the final tax clearance, board resolution, and audited financials prior to transferring funds to a foreign shareholder. For cross-strait flows involving Taiwan, the transactions are treated as foreign-exchange dealings; the New Taiwan Dollar is not a freely convertible onshore currency, and settlements must be denominated in CNY, USD, or another convertible currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds under current SAFE rules. A WFOE may retain 100 percent of goods- and service-trade export proceeds in a foreign-currency account or settle them into RMB at will. However, all export receipts must be repatriated to a domestic account within the commercial payment term agreed with the buyer, normally not exceeding 180 days, and must be entered into SAFE's Trade Collection, Verification, and Monitoring System without unreconciled arrears. For processing and kitting arrangements, the WFOE must demonstrate that the value of exported finished goods corresponds to the declared processing fees and the imported components; any overdue export collections from Taiwan counterparties must be reported to the local branch of SAFE, with supporting evidence of collection efforts, contract terms, and customs declarations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary cross-border payment and treasury-optimization flows, Low for serving as the sole corporate treasury account. Offshore EMIs such as Airwallex are not licensed PRC deposit-taking institutions and cannot hold a WFOE's SAFE-registered capital settlement account or satisfy the statutory corporate account requirements. They may be used to collect international marketplace settlements, pay foreign suppliers, and execute FX conversion through licensed partners, but the WFOE must maintain a domestic bank account for tax payments, salaries, and SAFE verification. Legal constraints require full transparency of the underlying trade documents and the use of a PBOC-licensed payment institution in the settlement chain for onshore RMB activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the legal representative or a senior authorized director, together with the company chop, original business license, articles of association, SAFE foreign-exchange registration, and all beneficial-ownership declarations, is mandatory for onboarding at tier-1 Chinese commercial banks. Telephone or video-conference interviews are not accepted as a substitute for foreign-owned entities; some banks permit a remotely interviewed and notarized power of attorney, but will require an in-person meeting with the local finance manager or a designated officer before activating the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated WFOE with a 100 percent foreign parent and a business scope limited to kitting, packing, and assembly, which may be perceived as a potential shell-company structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company business license, articles of association, parent-entity audited financial statements, executed client supply and fulfillment agreements, third-party warehouse lease or sub-contracted warehousing agreement, inventory movement reports, customs import/export records, employee payroll and social-security contribution reports, and a written operational narrative with projected unit economics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile resembling money pass-through or payment intermediation, such as high-frequency compact-value wires from unrelated e-commerce platforms or Taiwan-based customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with each customer, itemized commercial invoices, packing lists, bill of lading or air waybill records, customs clearing certificates, proof of value-added kitting procedures, cost-breakdown calculations evidencing a genuine service margin, intercompany or third-party transaction flow charts with bank statements, and monthly tax filings rendered to the local tax authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments routed through an offshore EMI or involving a Taiwan counterparty, particularly where the beneficial owner resides in a non-treaty or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership register with passport and proof-of-address documentation, SAFE foreign-exchange registration certificate, board resolutions approving the treasury structure, cross-strait service and product sales contracts, customs verification receipts, non-resident enterprise tax registration and withholding certificates for any service fee, and a formal AML/CTF compliance self-assessment with external legal opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent trade documents, where the declared kitting assembly fees do not match the physical movement of goods or the value of related inbound raw-material imports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full processing trade records under the customs supervision manual, reconciliation of imported components to exported finished goods, unit-production consumption tables, warehouse inbound/outbound logs, quality-control and inspection reports, carrier bills, SAFE trade-detail reporting, and a certified public accountant's report confirming revenue recognition under the prevailing accounting standards.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas parent shall remit the subscription capital by SWIFT MT103 into the WFOE's SAFE-registered Capital Settlement Account opened with a tier-1 domestic bank. The remittance reference field must identify the payment as FDI capital injection and quote the corresponding SAFE registration code. The receiving bank will verify the SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration Certificate, enter the transaction into SAFE's digital registration system, and then credit the foreign-currency capital account. Subsequent conversion into RMB for lawful operational purposes must comply with the posted capital-account usage restrictions; funds may not be used for equity investment, borrowing, securities investment, or real-estate acquisition outside the permitted scope. For Taiwan-sourced investment, payment should be wired in CNY, USD, or another freely convertible currency; TWD-denominated remittances cannot be credited onshore without prior conversion through the Taiwanese bank and a suitable clearing route.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine operating expenditures are cleared through the WFOE's RMB basic account using standard CNY transfers. For foreign-currency disbursements, including payments to Taiwan-based suppliers, subcontractors, or logistics partners, the WFOE will direct its bank to execute a SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer out of the designated foreign-currency operating account. For cross-border trade with Taiwan, the WFOE may alternatively use the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) to settle invoiced amounts in CNY, thereby reducing currency conversion costs. Where open-account terms are not agreed, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit may be issued by the WFOE's account bank; settlement will require presentation of commercial invoice, transport documents, packing list, and, where applicable, customs declarations. For service-trade outbound payments, the WFOE must first withhold and pay the relevant PRC taxes (including non-resident enterprise income tax and VAT on service importation), obtain the local tax authority's payment certificate, and submit it to the bank with the service agreement and invoice before the remittance is executed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards (remote settlement versus RMB) with genuine underlying current-account or approved capital-account exposure.
Onshore FX options and combination structures, including zero-cost collars and risk reversals, executed with a licensed PRC bank.
Onshore FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps used to match working-capital cash flows or to hedge long-term trade payables and receivables.
Cross-border RMB settlement through CIPS and the onshore CNY FX market used as a settlement and hedging mechanism for Taiwan-related transactions.
Offshore RMB NDFs are not permissible for onshore WFOEs; any proposed NDF structure should be replaced by an onshore deliverable forward or a CIPS-denominated CNY settlement mechanism.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the fifth month after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a surcharge generally based on tax payable, statutory fines, interest, and estimated assessment. Taiwan has no automatic annual franchise strike-off solely for late filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year, unless an approved extension applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may face administrative fines and liability for losses caused by non-compliance. No routine government filing fee applies unless a registration change is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding and non-resident income reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 31 January for the preceding calendar year, subject to the applicable withholding category and reporting method.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or inaccurate reporting may result in withholding-tax assessments, interest, administrative fines, and penalties imposed on the withholding agent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register and beneficial ownership review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; information may be requested by the Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent AML authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Complete before the annual shareholders' meeting and update promptly after any shareholding, director, manager, or beneficial ownership change. Taiwan generally has no separate annual UBO confirmation filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or provide required ownership information may result in administrative fines, corrective orders, and AML or company-law enforcement. No automatic annual strike-off applies solely to an internal register review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Taiwan VAT returns are generally filed bimonthly by the 15th day of the following odd-numbered month; confirm completion of all six annual periods.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment may trigger late-payment interest, administrative fines, tax assessment, and restrictions on tax-credit claims.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is generally required for public companies and for private companies meeting applicable Taiwan thresholds, including paid-in capital of at least NT$30 million, annual net operating revenue of at least NT$100 million, or an average workforce of at least 100 employees, subject to current tax and company-law rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for private companies; Taiwan-IFRS is generally required for listed, OTC, and other designated public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is generally no standalone annual UBO certification for a Taiwan private company. Review and reconcile the Register of Shareholders, director and manager information, control structure, and beneficial ownership annually; report legally required changes within the applicable registration or AML deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 800-2,500 per year, depending on office services, mail handling, nominee support, and filing volume.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-10,000 for a small private company; higher for regulated, complex, or threshold-triggered entities.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate 25%. Preferential rates available: (i) 15% for High-and-New-Technology Enterprises (HNTE) and encouraged industries in the Western Regions (2021–2030); (ii) effective 5% for Small-and-Low-Profit Enterprises (annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million) until 31 December 2027; (iii) super-deductions: 100% additional deduction for R&D expenses (2023–2025 policy window extended); (iv) no general tax holiday for standard kitting/3PL activities. Small-value 'zero' preferential treatment for micro-enterprises under local surcharges may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (Form A), Form A100000 with mandatory general schedules (A105000, A106000, A107040 et al.) under the unified 'Annual Declaration of Enterprise Income Tax' system; e-filed via the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (国家税务总局电子税务局) using digital certificate (UKEY) or direct login.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, with quarterly provisional (prepayment) returns due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end; annual reconciliation within 5 months after the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 December fiscal year-end: annual return and final payment by 31 May of the following year (5 months after year-end); quarterly prepayments by 15 January, 15 April, 15 July and 15 October respectively.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form A100000, Line 1 – 营业收入 (Revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book revenue from warehousing, kitting, packaging and fulfillment-3PL services recognized under PRC Accounting Standards; gross of VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan-region investor is not a party to the WFOE's annual return; the return is submitted by the WFOE as the resident taxpayer. No non-resident signature or disclosure is required on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form A100000, Line 2 – 营业成本 (Cost of Sales)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs: wages, warehouse leasing, consumables, subcontracting of kitting labor, inbound freight (third-party) and packaging materials; must reconcile to the general ledger.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany costs from the Taiwan parent must be backed by contemporaneous TP documentation; otherwise the tax authority may add back or re-price.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form A100000, Line 10 – 利润总额 (Total Accounting Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax derived by adding operating profit, non-operating income and non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no line-level filing role; profit of the WFOE remains subject to full CIT before distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form A100000, Line 11 – 纳税调整增加额 (Tax Adjustment Increases)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of book-to-tax differences: disallowed entertainment, improper invoices, excess 'related-party service' fees, fines, provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees charged by the Taiwan parent not linked to actual services are non-deductible; the entry must provide explicit support to resist a re-characterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form A100000, Line 19 – 应纳税所得额 (Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income = Total Accounting Profit + adjustments – exempt/deducted/super-deducted amounts; minimum may not be artificially reduced below arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has taken a treaty-based interest/royalty deduction to the Taiwan parent, the payable WHT consequences must be disclosed in the withholding returns, not in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form A100000, Lines 20–30 – Rate, Tax Payable, Credits and Balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 20 auto-fills 25%; Line 22 computes EIT payable; Line 23 applies reduced rates (e.g., 15% or 5%); Line 28/29 creditable foreign taxes; Line 30 actual payable; Lines 31–34 refund/additional payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annual return settles only the WFOE's CIT; dividend WHT (10%, treaty-reduced to 5%) is withheld and remitted separately by the WFOE at the time of actual distribution to the Taiwan shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory schedule capturing interest expenses, service fees, royalties and other intercompany payments; cross-checked against the annual transfer-pricing statement (Annual Reporting of Related-Party Transactions, Form G100000/GB series).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must file the annual related-party transaction report (2016 Announcement No. 42) disclosing all transactions with the Taiwan parent, including the 15% standard intercompany service margin benchmark expectation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing or late filing: administrative fine of RMB 2,000–10,000 (Tax Administration Law Art. 62); late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax (Art. 32); understatement resulting from tax evasion: fine of 50%–500% of the underpaid tax (Art. 63); for withholding violations on dividends/royalties/interest: 50%–300% of the un-collected/un-remitted amount (Art. 69). Criminal referral applies where tax evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax payable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends distributed by the WFOE to the non-resident Taiwan-region shareholder (Enterprise Income Tax Law Art. 37; SAT Announcement 2017 No. 37 on the time of deemed payment).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Enhancement of Tax Cooperation (signed 25 August 2015; in force since 28 August 2020) reduces the mainland-source dividend WHT to 5% where the Taiwan beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25% of the WFOE's capital (subject to the agreement's holding-condition requirement), or to 10% in other cases. Procedure: (1) obtain a Taiwan Tax Resident Certificate (居住者證明) from the competent Taiwan tax administration; (2) the Taiwan shareholder completes the non-resident treaty-benefit self-declaration and BO form under SAT Announcement 2019 No. 35 and satisfies the 'beneficial owner' factors of SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9 (no shell/conduit, substantive business activity, control and risk of the shares); (3) the WFOE withholds at the reduced rate and retain supporting documents for at least 10 years; (4) the tax authority may re-verify; if relief is fraudulently claimed, the difference plus 50%–300% penalty and interest apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on mainland-source interest and royalties: 10% on the gross amount (EIT Law Art. 37). Under the Cross-Strait Agreement, the source-state cap is 7% of the gross amount for interest paid by the WFOE to a Taiwan-region financial institution/beneficial owner and 7% for royalties (inclusive of software and know-how licensing); domestic 6% VAT and 12% local surcharges may apply on royalties depending on taxability, and service fees of a non-royalty nature are subject to 10% WHT only if attributable to an establishment, otherwise CIT exposure typically via deemed-profit.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous TP documentation (Local File/Master File) is mandatory where prior-year related-party transactions reach any of these RMB thresholds (SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42): tangible-asset transfers ≥ RMB 400 million; intangible-asset transfers ≥ RMB 100 million; financial-asset transfers ≥ RMB 100 million; related-party services ≥ RMB 100 million; Master File is required where prior-year aggregate related-party revenue exceeds RMB 2 billion. In addition, an annual related-party transaction reporting form (including G100000 and GB/TW schedules) must be attached to the annual EIT return regardless of the amounts.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: mainland China does not apply the offshore ESR (Economic Substance Regulations) regime, but enforces the substance-over-form doctrine through: (i) general anti-avoidance rule (EIT Law Art. 47; Implementation Regulation Arts. 120–123) allowing re-characterization of any structure without reasonable commercial purpose; (ii) beneficial-ownership test for treaty relief (SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9, seven settled factors incl. actual operations, employment, decision-making and risk-bearing); (iii) place-of-effective-management classification of Chinese-tax-resident status; and (iv) the Special Tax Investigation and Adjustment rules requiring attribution of profits to functions performed, assets utilized and risks assumed. The WFOE must demonstrate physical premises, operational staff, actual kitting/fulfillment activity and bank/accounting records to preserve treaty benefits and resist a GAAR adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fictitious Invoicing (虚开发票)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting fake VAT special/general invoices for kitting, packing or warehousing services without real transactions; under-recording cash revenue; inflating intercompany labor or packaging costs; round-tripping funds through the Taiwan parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Law Arts. 63/66: fine of 50%–500% of the evaded tax; Criminal Law Art. 201 (tax evasion): up to 7 years' imprisonment plus fines for the entity's responsible persons where the evaded amount is huge; Criminal Law Art. 205 (fictitious VAT invoices): up to life imprisonment and confiscation for particularly large amounts; deregistration of VAT qualifications and reputational debarment from e-commerce export programs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, financial officer and actual de facto controllers face criminal liability (criminal fines and imprisonment); civil restitution to the tax authority for the state's loss; administrative exit bans under Tax Administration Law Art. 44 and Exit-Entry Administration Law Art. 12 (travel ban); disqualification as officers; in case of unit crime, the enterprise is fined and the 'directly responsible personnel' are prosecuted in person.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Letterbox Entity with No Substantive Operation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: WFOE maintained solely to channel Taiwan-region profits, with no genuine fulfillment activity: zero operational employees, no warehouse premises, absence of decision-making, all capital operations outsourced to the parent; nominee or foreign-appointed directors without authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Company Law (2023, effective 1 July 2024) Art. 23: piercing the veil where shareholder abuse of independence causes severe corporate damage or creditors' harm — joint and several personal liability; GAAR re-characterization under EIT Law Art. 47 with supplementary tax and compensatory interest at the PBOC benchmark rate plus 5 percentage points; market supervision deregistration and revoking of the WFOE license; TP 'top-up' adjustments to the Taiwan parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and de facto controllers jointly and unlimitedly liable to the tax authority and trade creditors; director liability for false financial reporting; added exit restrictions where the entity owes tax; criminal exposure if the shell is used to defraud tax refunds or cross-border settlement systems.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Illegal Fund Settlement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the fulfillment entity as a fund pass-through for third-party cross-border payments, accepting client proceeds without customer due diligence, bundling unrelated e-commerce sales, using underground banks to repatriate, or splitting large-volume transactions to avoid reporting thresholds in connection with ACH/Airwallex rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (effective 1 January 2025): institution-level fines up to RMB 5 million, alongside confiscation of illegal gains and suspension/license revocation; Criminal Law Art. 191 (money laundering): up to 10 years' imprisonment plus fines for individuals; failure to perform KYC/Odds reporting responsibilities triggers supervisory penalties and 'blacklist' designation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior management and compliance officers face personal administrative fines and prohibition orders; directors who knowingly participate are criminally liable with confiscation; issuance of asset-freeze orders and cross-border travel bans; the corporate veil may be pierced to pursue controlling shareholders for consequential damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Disclosure and Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the annual related-party transaction statement; levying excessive management fees, trademark or software royalties from the Taiwan parent with no function-and-risk justification; adopting a residual-profit split favoring the parent; not maintaining Local File despite threshold breaches; systematic thin capitalization exceeding the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio (5:1 for financial industries).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustments with compensatory interest at the PBOC benchmark rate plus 5 percentage points from the filing deadline (Implementation Regulation Art. 48); penalty for non-compliance with documentation: RMB 2,000–10,000 administratively, presumption of adjustment, and re-characterization of the transactions; exchange-of-information cross-checks under the Cross-Strait Agreement; in cases of fraudulent pricing, application of the 50%–500% evasion fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where fraudulent pricing is found, the directors responsible for signing and certifying the tax returns are exposed to criminal proceedings; the tax authority may seek civil recovery of the tax shortfall from the shareholders receiving the benefit; exit bans and property preservations apply pending payment; management may be disqualified from serving as directors of other Chinese enterprises.
